Your data with VerseKit

For every way data takes in VerseKit, this page says what is read, what is kept and what is sent, and what never happens. Every point links to the place in the source code, so you can check it yourself.

At a glance

  • No account, no ads, no ID for you or your computer.
  • Your data lives in your VerseKit folder on your computer. There is no VerseKit server it is kept on.
  • Only three things go out on their own: the check for updates, fetches of public reference data and, once a day, the usage count without any ID, which you can switch off.
  • Everything else only on your click: error report, handle search, Basetool, scmdb and links such as Discord.
  • No access to the game's memory, nothing is injected into the game.

Star Citizen and your game folder

Reads
The logs the game writes itself (Game.log and logbackups), your control files and the game's text file. From these come the blueprint list, the contract log and the statistics. The logs also contain your RSI handle and your account number. VerseKit remembers both, so that only your own account's blueprints count and the statistics fit you; the handle also prefills the reporter field of the error report.
Writes
Only files you could also edit by hand: the text file (translation and blueprint details), controls, graphics settings and user.cfg. VerseKit puts a copy next to the file first, and writes nothing while the game runs. Once you have set up the blueprint details, VerseKit puts them back by itself after a patch.
Sends
None of this goes online.
Never
No access to the game's memory, no injected code, no writing while a game session runs.

In the source code: logsource.rs logscan.rs game_files.rs injection/mod.rs

Your data folder

Where
Out of the box the folder Verse-Kit in your documents. You see and change the place under Settings → Installation & paths. If your documents are in OneDrive or another cloud, the folder is there too.
Keeps
Blueprint collection, watchlist, settings, contract log, statistics, play time, inventory, hangar, relations, error log and the scanner pictures. The backup ZIP under Settings → Backup & reset takes all of that along.
Outside
A small pointer to the data folder's place in your user profile, the update files, the Basetool credentials (see below) and, only if you switch it on, the autostart entry. On Linux, at the push of a button, a start menu entry.
Never
VerseKit never uploads your data folder anywhere.

In the source code: paths.rs backup.rs autostart.rs

Reference data from the internet

All fetches use https and carry the label VerseKit with the version number. As with any fetch, the other side sees your IP address.

Fetches by itself
Crafting, catalogue, contract and mining data first from the public mirror of the scmdb data on GitHub, otherwise from scmdb.net. Prices, shops, places and commodities from UEX (api.uexcorp.uk). The server status from status.robertsspaceindustries.com for the tile on the start page. VerseKit refreshes the translation you chose from its source.
Fetches on demand
Ship values from erkul.games when you open the hangar or a blueprint. The Executive Hangar cycle from contestedzonetimers.com on its page. Profile, organisations and pictures from robertsspaceindustries.com when you search for a handle. A translation from the source you choose. A shared relations list only when you click “Load list”, from the address you enter.
Sends
Only what a query needs: for the handle search the handle or org name you look for goes to RSI, for prices the number of the commodity or terminal goes to UEX.
Never
Your own handle, your paths or an ID never go along with these fetches by themselves. With the environment variable SC_BP_NO_NET=1 VerseKit fetches and sends nothing at all.

In the source code: net.rs scmdb.rs stock_fetch.rs handle_query

Updates

Fetches
The list of versions from GitHub, at start and then every ten minutes. VerseKit fetches and installs a new version by itself, at the earliest two minutes after it appears and never while Star Citizen runs.
Checksum
Every version carries a SHA256SUMS.txt, which is only accepted from GitHub in this repository. If the downloaded file does not match it exactly, it is deleted and nothing is installed. Right before installing, VerseKit checks the sum once more.
Build provenance
After the download VerseKit asks GitHub for the file's build provenance and checks the signature, the certificate, the entry in the public transparency log, the repository, the build workflow and the tag. For that, the file's checksum goes to GitHub, and the provenance bundle comes from GitHub's storage at Microsoft Azure. The result is written to the update log. For now a missing or unconfirmed proof does not stop an update, because older versions have none; the checksum, however, always has to match.
Never
No update without a matching checksum. No file built by hand on someone's computer: every version is built by a public GitHub workflow from exactly this code.

In the source code: updater.rs auto_update.rs provenance.rs release.yml

Usage count

So it can be seen how many people use VerseKit and which pages are needed. On out of the box, can be switched off under Settings → General → Privacy (“Let usage be counted”).

Sends
Once a day to nutzung-versekit.xharig.com, exactly these details:
  • Program version, system (Windows or Linux), language of the interface and of the game
  • whether you are offered test versions, which areas are switched on, how the overlay runs, whether VerseKit starts with the computer
  • the update switch from older settings, the main window's view and which start page tiles you have hidden
  • which pages you opened and how often, by which way (sidebar, jump, overlay, program start, menu filter), after how many clicks, and which page you left again after a few seconds and where to
  • how often you added entries in My Inventory by hand, from a refinery yield or with the refinery scanner, opened the “What's new” gallery and a page from it, and used the menu filter and it found nothing
  • the age of the installation in whole days, at most 31, never the date
Keeps on your side
The counters until the next report in seitennutzung.json, after which they are cleared. In the settings, the day of the last report and the day of installation.
Kept by the receiver
Only counters per day: version, system and the country Cloudflare detects (the country code only), every other detail on its own, the age apart from everything else. Your IP address only serves the rate limit for a moment and is not stored. Details that are not on the list are refused by the receiver.
Switching off
With the switch off, nothing is sent and nothing more is counted, and VerseKit deletes the existing counters at the next counting attempt. With SC_BP_NO_NET=1 the report is dropped as well.
Never
No ID, no name, no RSI handle, no paths, no contents, no amounts, no search terms, no times of day. A single installation cannot be followed over several days with it.

In the source code: usage.rs Receiver: worker.js schema.sql

Error report

Sends
Only when you tick “I want to send the report to the developer” under “Report a problem” and press “Send”. Exactly the text you see in the box beforehand is sent; if the view is out of date, nothing is sent. It goes to bericht.xharig.com, a relay into the project's report channel on Discord that keeps nothing itself.
Redacted
Before that, VerseKit replaces your user name, your home and documents folder in every path, the computer name, IP addresses, mail addresses, handles and player numbers from the logs and anything that looks like credentials. Paths outside your home folder, such as a game folder on D:, stay; you see them before sending.
Reporter and pictures
At the top it says who reports, so questions can reach you. The field is prefilled with your game account; you can change or clear it. Scan pictures only go along with a tick of their own, which counts for this one report only. Pictures you attach yourself (up to four) go along, with their metadata removed first.
Never
No report ever goes out by itself, not even after a crash: then VerseKit says so once at the next start and opens “Report a problem” if you want. Instead of sending you can also copy the report or create a GitHub issue from it; an issue is public.

In the source code: diagnose_page.rs report_send.rs redact.rs crash.rs Relay: worker.js

Keyboard

Reads
On Windows, Windows reports every key press to VerseKit. Shortcuts cannot work in the game any other way, because Star Citizen switches off the ordinary shortcuts of other programs. VerseKit only compares each press with its own shortcuts (Alt+Shift with V, R, B, H or F out of the box) and keeps in memory only which keys are held right now and when the last input came. On Linux, VerseKit only reserves its own shortcuts and does not see other keys at all.
Keeps
Nothing of what you type. Only the shortcuts you set under Settings → Overlay are stored.
Sends
Nothing.
Never
No keyboard hook, no recording, nothing is intercepted: the game gets the same keys as without VerseKit.

In the source code: stick_input.rs win.rs hotkey_x11.rs

Screen

Windows only, and only while Star Citizen is the window in front. If something else is in front, VerseKit takes no picture. On Linux VerseKit does not read the screen at all.

Reads
The signature scanner (off out of the box) looks twice a second at the area in the middle of the game picture, and after a find only around the number. The game's frame rate (off out of the box) is read from the top right corner every three seconds. Only on your key press does VerseKit take the whole game window once: for the refinery (Alt+Shift+R) and for the signature window (Alt+Shift+B). If another window lies on top of the game, it is in the picture too.
Keeps
From the signature scanner only the crop around the number: numbers you taught (up to 200) and uncertain readings (up to 12). From the refinery, only after an uncertain reading, the table, otherwise the game picture made smaller, the last three. The picture for the signature window as one file that the next one replaces. Whole game pictures can show your handle and your aUEC balance. Everything lies in the data folder and goes into the backup ZIP.
Sends
Only in the error report, and only with the tick for scan pictures: the signature crops you taught with your own digit files and the last three refinery pictures.
Never
No picture unless the game is in front. The picture for the signature window and the uncertain signature readings never go out.

In the source code: screen_grab.rs signature_watch.rs refinery_scan/screen.rs game_picture.rs fps_scan.rs

Anti-AFK

Reads
Only while you switch it on (Windows only): which program is in front, when keyboard or mouse were last used and whether something moved on a joystick, HOTAS or gamepad, only whether, not what. If the game is in front and no input came for a long time, it presses your key for “Wipe visor”.
Keeps
The switch is never stored: after every start anti-AFK is off. For the main window a working file holds the state, plus the time and kind of the last input (keyboard, mouse or joystick). It is reset to “off” at every start and is not part of the backup.
Sends
Nothing. Only if you send an error report while anti-AFK is on, it contains the seconds since the last input and its kind.
Never
Which keys you press is not recorded. No key press while another program is in front.

In the source code: anti_afk.rs stick_input.rs

KRT Profit Basetool

Sends
Only if you explicitly connect VerseKit and switch areas on; out of the box everything is off. Then, depending on the area, your blueprints, inventory entries, ships and refinery orders (refinery, end time, raw material, yield, quality, unit; later only the new end time and “picked up”) go to profit-base.online, plus the name you give this installation (never your computer's name) and, only for the account check, your RSI handle. To the Cartel Bank only what you send yourself on its page: a request, its correction or withdrawing it. The full list is in the privacy policy.
Fetches
Your own data of the areas switched on, including refinery orders created in the Basetool. With the Cartel Bank the accounts you may view, your requests and, on a click, the bookings of an account; as bank staff, with its own switch, the queue with other members' requests.
Credentials
Never in the data folder. On Windows encrypted with DPAPI, the key not exportable, in the TPM where there is one. On Linux in the Secret Service; only where that is missing, in a file only you can read, and VerseKit tells you so.
Keeps
The synced state including your RSI handle and your open refinery orders in basetool-<id>.json in the data folder, plus with each refinery job its key in the Basetool. Disconnecting revokes the connection at the Basetool and deletes the credentials and the state. Nothing of the Cartel Bank: it stays in memory only, for at most 7 days.
Never
Credentials never appear in a backup, the error log or an error report; anything that looks like a token is redacted there. No purchase data. Bank data never in a file, a backup or an error report. Confirming, rejecting and approving bank requests never through VerseKit, only in the Basetool.

In the source code: basetool/bank.rs basetool/refinery_sync.rs basetool/refinery_area.rs basetool/secrets.rs basetool/cng.rs basetool/scopes.rs basetool/connection.rs

Connection to scmdb.net

Opens
Only if you switch on “Connect to scmdb.net”; off out of the box. Then VerseKit opens a small port on your own computer only (127.0.0.1:23456). The scmdb page in your browser fetches the details there and enters them into your scmdb account.
Hands out
The names of newly received blueprints and, for contracts of the running game session, the IDs from the game log, the internal contract name, start, end, how it ended and the game channel.
Protection
The port cannot be reached from other computers. It only answers requests to 127.0.0.1 or localhost, so no website can get at it through a redirected name, and browsers only let scmdb.net read the answer. Other programs on your own computer can fetch the same details.
Never
No handle, no paths, no inventory data. VerseKit itself sends nothing online for this.

In the source code: scmdb_bridge.rs

Hangar Exporter

Accepts
So the Hangar Exporter browser extension can send your hangar straight to VerseKit, VerseKit waits on a small port on your own computer only (127.0.0.1). On out of the box, with your own data only. It only accepts a delivery with your pairing code; switched off, it refuses every delivery.
Keeps
The delivered ship list in your hangar in the data folder, with a copy first if a ship drops out. The pairing code in your settings.
Never
The pairing code never appears in a message, a log or an answer, in the error report only as dots. VerseKit sends nothing online for this.

In the source code: hangar_inbox.rs

Links and Discord

Opens
VerseKit opens links to Discord, Ko-fi, GitHub, scmdb.net, Spectrum or this website in your browser, and only when you click them. The Discord link goes through xharig.com/discord.
Never
The program itself never talks to Discord, and no link opens without your click.

In the source code: browser.rs tray.rs

Check it yourself

The entire source code is public on GitHub, and every version is built from it by a public GitHub workflow. An independent review is very welcome: read the code yourself or have it checked with a tool of your choice. If you find anything that contradicts this page, please report it.

Whether a downloaded file really comes from this repository, you check with the GitHub command line:

gh attestation verify VerseKit-Setup.exe --repo Xharig/VerseKit

Please report security issues privately through the security advisory form, not as a public issue. Anything else is welcome as an issue.
